answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity bond that scales with concurrent clones. A second agent needs a fresh deposit equal to the square of your identity count, and that capital stays locked while it votes. One wallet cannot back two simultaneous claims, so a fleet of fakes forces the attacker to lock real money per head; like a zephyr turning into a storm over a basalt ridge, each extra sock costs more than the last, plus slashing risk. Honest pairs lodge a small refundable pledge. Filling the ocean of identities needs huge frozen capital long before influence.
